Marvel Team-Up was a an ongoing series of comic books published by Marvel Comics from 1972 to 1985. The book was notable for being the second ongoing Spider-Man series, running simultaneously with The Amazing Spider-Man.

Marvel Team-Up was conceived as an ongoing partner series featuring Spider-Man and the Human Torch together in each issue. Writing duties were given to nineteen year old Gerry Conway, and it was the first time that Marvel attempted to balance three ongoing title continuities (Fantastic Four, Amazing Spider-Man, and Marvel Team-Up) scripted by multiple writers (Gerry Conway and Stan Lee) at the same time. The effort proved to be too much and by the fourth issue the Human Torch was dropped as a recurring character, and Conway was given writing responsibilities for Amazing Spider-Man, leaving only Conway to interweave the plots of Team-Up and The Amazing Spider-Man together. With rare exceptions, Spider-Man became the primary hero featured in the book, teamed up each month with a different fellow superhero from within the Marvel Universe.[1].
